newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Wednesday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange with many investors offsetting their positions before China's National Day holiday, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,110 yuan ($2,422) per tonne, rising 190 yuan. It opened at 20,150 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,080 and a high of 20,200.
October rose 10 to 20,460 yuan, November 90 to 20,240, December 190 to 20,150, February 200 to 20,100, March 170 to 20,130 and April 240 to 20,150.
Combined volume rose to 32,740 tonnes from 21,430.
Copper opened up and moved at that level for most of the session.
Traders said that LME copper breaching the key $1,900 resistance level last night triggered short-covering in Shanghai and pushed all the later-maturing contracts above 20,000 yuan.
"Short-covering was responsible for today's rises but investors lost short-term direction due to a consolidation on the LME after the breach of the $1,900 level," one trader said.
"The open interest of most contracts fell. Investors do not want to hold positions during the National Day holiday," he added. The holiday lasts from Sept 30 to Oct 3.
Traders said that the LME was still a major factor influencing Shanghai copper because of a lack of domestic market-moving news.
"Copper will follow LME's trend in the next few days with many investors continuing to liquidate their positions with the approach of the holiday," a second trader said.
Analysts said that copper was likely to test the 20,000-yuan support level in the short term.
